title: App
line: What app({ ... }) takes. Every function is pure: same input, same output; the world reaches it only through its arguments.

id.line: Names the folder and every verb: id.verb.

line.line: One sentence: what the app is for.

boot.line: ({ seed, start, config, actors, knob }) => state. Runs once, when a world boots.

verbs.line: name: { line, args?, inner?, guest?, run }. guest lets a person outside the actors list act. line is a string, or (knob) => string. args is a JSON schema, or (knob) => schema; never from state. inner verbs run only when an app or the host asks. run(state, args, ctx) returns the next state.

read.line: (state, path, who, at, peek) => view. What who sees at path, live at time at. peek(path) is any app's raw state, a copy. Default: the state itself.

moves.line: (state) => names. Which verbs are legal now. Default: all.

knobs.line: name: { line, schema, reality }. Everything that shapes a world. A world turns one with the rule id.name; reality fills the rest.

wake.line: (state, at) => verb | null. The inner verb to run when time alone changed this app. The host asks around each act and journals what runs.

after.line: ({ world, envelope, line }) => act | null. Watch another app's act, and follow it with one of your own; it runs as the same who, via this app.

hear.line: (state, line) => state. Every journal line as it lands, refused acts too. It draws nothing and acts on nothing, so a replay rebuilds it and the journal never changes.

view.line: What to show, as plain JSON, in order. value { from, as, title }, rows { from, fields, title?, reverse? }, form { verb, rank, choices? }, chart { from, x, y, shape, title?, xunit?, skip? }, viewer { name }, do { action, title, to?, sure? }, group { nodes, title?, needs? }, pref { key, as, title, options?, on?, off?, art? }, pane { id, title, nodes }. from is { world: path } or { file: url, path? }, where * in a file path walks every key; a field is { key, as, title?, unit?, names? }; a field or value may add unit, a word after the number, and a field may add names, a source that maps ids to names; as is text, number, time or person; rank is primary, secondary or rare; rows take a list; choices map an arg to one source or a list of them, each a map of ids to names or a list. Any node with guest false hides from guests. The kernel and doors ignore it; the browser draws it. Default: the state as a tree and every verb as a form.

ctx.line: who, at, via; draw() a random 32-bit number; refuse(note) undoes the act; say(value) answers the caller; see(path) reads as who; read(path) reads raw state; call(verb, args) runs another app's verb inside this act, and its refusal undoes the whole act; wish({ kind, data, reply }) asks the outside, and the answer returns as the inner verb reply with args { wish, ok, data }; knob(name) reads a knob, yours by name or anyone's as app.name.
